### Key takeaways


- Identity governance and administration (IGA) is a policy-based approach to identity security that combines day-to-day identity administration (provisioning, credential management) with continuous governance (access reviews, compliance auditing, segregation of duties).
- While traditional identity and access management controls how users sign in, IGA governs *what* users can access, *why* they have that access, and *whether* those permissions remain compliant over time.


Identity governance and administration (IGA) is a policy-based approach to identity management and access control. As the name implies, IGA systems merge identity governance and identity administration to provide additional functionality beyond traditional identity and access management (IAM) tools. Particularly, they offer valuable support in auditing and meeting compliance requirements.


IGA systems can also help[automate workflows](https://www.okta.com/products/workflows/) for provisioning and deprovisioning users. This is especially important given the growing need for users to sign in from any location and on any device, which makes IAM more difficult to manage.


An IGA framework consists of two core pillars:


-


**Identity governance:** Policy enforcement processes covering segregation of duties, role-based access control (RBAC), logging, access certifications and reviews, analytics, and compliance reporting


-


**Identity administration:** Operational lifecycle tasks including account and credential management, automated user and device provisioning and deprovisioning, and entitlement management


While an IGA solution makes a lot of sense for most organizations, implementing it can be difficult and time-consuming. As such, it’s important to fully understand[what IGA is](https://www.okta.com/blog/industry-insights/your-guide-to-modern-identity-governance/) before getting started. So, let’s get started.


## What’s the difference between IGA and IAM?


While IGA and IAM go hand in hand, they’re not the same thing. IGA goes beyond standard[IAM systems](https://www.okta.com/blog/identity-security/modern-identity-at-work-productivity-meets-security/) by helping businesses administer identities, meet compliance requirements, and audit processes for compliance reporting.


Feature/capability Identity and access management (IAM) Identity governance and administration (IGA)


Primary function Authenticates users and grants real-time access (single sign-on, multi-factor authentication) Governs access policies, audits permissions, and enforces compliance


Core focus Operational access (“Can this user sign in right now?”) Visibility and risk (“Should this user still have this access?”)


Lifecycle management Basic account creation and authentication Automated provisioning and deprovisioning


Compliance and auditing Basic sign-in logs Automated access reviews, segregation of duties, and audit trails


## The core components of an IGA solution


Modern IGA platforms integrate with existing IAM infrastructure to automate five critical[identity lifecycle](https://www.okta.com/products/lifecycle-management/) functions:


- **Centralized password and credential policy enforcement:** Works alongside[single sign-on](https://www.okta.com/products/single-sign-on-workforce-identity/) and password management tools to enforce credential hygiene across hybrid environments
- **Automated lifecycle workflows:** Automates[onboarding (provisioning), role changes, and offboarding (deprovisioning)](https://www.okta.com/blog/industry-insights/scaling-identity-lifecycle-with-okta-identity-governance/) so permissions update immediately when an employee joins, moves, or leaves
- **Granular entitlement and permission management:** Defines and verifies specific actions users can take inside individual applications using[RBAC and least-privilege principles](https://www.okta.com/blog/industry-insights/simplifying-role-based-access-control-at-scale/)
- **Compliance reporting and analytics:** Generates audit-ready logs and risk analytics required to satisfy industry-specific and general data-focused regulations
- **Continuous access reviews and certifications:** Streamlines periodic verification of user permissions across cloud-based and on-premises apps to eliminate privilege creep


These components work together to enhance how you manage identity.


## How has identity governance and administration evolved?


The demand for IGA solutions emerged alongside stringent data regulations such as the[Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX)](https://www.okta.com/identity-101/iam-compliance/) and the[Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)](https://www.okta.com/hipaa/) , which required improved transparency and data management. To support these efforts, IGA systems provide organizations with better visibility into identity and access privileges and stronger controls to detect and prevent inappropriate access to their resources.


Gartner recognized the importance of IGA security in 2012, naming it the fastest-growing sector of the identity management market. Then, in 2013, the analyst house launched its first[Magic Quadrant for Identity Governance and Administration](https://www.gartner.com/en/documents/3970173/magic-quadrant-for-identity-governance-and-administratio) , which merged its two existing Identity Governance and Identity Administration categories, further solidifying Identity Governance and Administration as a priority for organizations.

## Myth vs. fact: Common myths about identity governance


While IGA is a key part of a robust IAM solution, there are many misconceptions around what it looks like in practice:


### Myth: IGA solutions are only available on-premises


**Fact:** Modern IGA platforms are cloud-native and cross-domain, managing access certifications,[automated provisioning](https://www.okta.com/blog/industry-insights/provisioning-made-simple-with-okta-identity-governance/) , and[entitlements](https://www.okta.com/blog/industry-insights/why-entitlement-management-needs-a-modern-take/) across both SaaS/cloud applications and legacy on-premises systems.


### Myth: IGA can’t manage cloud applications


**Fact:** Leading IGA solutions offer rich connectivity options for businesses to unify cloud and on-premises resources. All identity governance capabilities are cross-domain, which means they can be used to manage both cloud and on-premises applications.


### Myth: Organizations without strict regulatory mandates don’t need IGA


**Fact:** Identity governance is critical to[any security strategy](https://www.okta.com/blog/industry-insights/enabling-security-driven-governance/) regardless of industry. Hackers are constantly on the lookout for user credentials to steal, which makes it crucial for businesses to keep malicious actors out of their corporate systems. Regardless of whether a business needs to comply with regulations,[IGA enforces least-privilege access](https://www.okta.com/identity-101/how-identity-governance-protects-your-business/) to protect user accounts and prevent lateral movement during a breach.


### Myth: IGA is only relevant for large enterprises


**Fact:** Any organization experiencing high access-request volume or rapid headcount scaling benefits from automated provisioning, which prevents IT bottlenecks and establishes early security hygiene. For small businesses looking to scale, implementing IGA processes can help ensure they are proactively compliant with regulations that might target larger companies.


## When does an organization need an IGA solution?


There are several benefits to implementing an IGA solution:


- Timely access to the resources users need
- The ability to manage access requests and oversee risk
- Meet service-level requirements without compromising security, using automated policy enforcement
- Verify that the right controls are in place to meet security and privacy requirements stipulated by ever-stricter data regulations


But does your organization need an IGA solution? While your instinct might be to make this decision based on the size of your workforce, IT leaders should evaluate three operational triggers to determine if they need IGA:


- **High ticket volume:** Your team is bottlenecked by[manual access requests, role changes, and onboarding/offboarding tickets](https://www.okta.com/blog/industry-insights/fast--policy-driven-access-requests-without-the-manual-headaches/)
- **Audit and compliance friction:** Preparing for[security audits](https://www.okta.com/blog/industry-insights/end-to-end-visibility-for-governance-and-compliance/) or[periodic access certifications](https://www.okta.com/blog/industry-insights/modernizing-access-reviews-with-okta/) requires manual spreadsheets and weeks of administrative effort
- **Hybrid app sprawl:** Employees access dozens of[cloud and on-premises apps](https://www.okta.com/blog/industry-insights/simplifying-governance-on-prem-apps/) , creating visibility gaps and orphaned accounts


An IGA solution eases pressure on the IT team, enabling the business to[automate workflows](https://www.okta.com/blog/customers-and-partners/okta-workflows-identity-security/) that provision access requests by role and process bulk approvals. Regardless of organization size, it’s important to recognize the importance of security and be aware of the risk of breaches arising from gaps between incorrect access and security concerns.
